content: For adults weighing 5 kg, administer 1,000 units per kilogram per day intramuscularly, divided into doses every 8 to 12 hours. For children, administer 800 to 1,200 units per kilogram per day, divided into doses every 8 hours. Administer the intramuscular injection in the upper outer quadrant of the buttocks, alternating between the right and left sides. Avoid giving multiple injections in the same region. Be aware of potential nephrotoxic reactions, which may include albuminuria, cylindruria, and azotemia. Nausea and vomiting are possible side effects. Itching may occur as an adverse reaction. Blood dyscrasias, such as abnormalities in blood cell counts, may develop. Patients may experience diaphoresis (excessive sweating). Pain at the injection site is a common side effect. Skin rashes and hypersensitivity reactions may occur. Do not administer this medication intravenously, as severe thrombophlebitis could result. Prescribing this medication in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection, or without a prophylactic indication, may not benefit the patient and could contribute to the development of bacterial resistance. Ensure the patient maintains adequate fluid intake during treatment. Antibiotics may lead to the overgrowth of organisms that are not susceptible to the drug, including fungi. This medication is classified as Pregnancy Category C, meaning that risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. It is unknown whether this medication is excreted in breast milk during lactation. Pregnancy Category A indicates that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
